pr.title: Reload an instrument's voice when its program is saved, and give voices the modulation wheel (keyboard-instrument.md §14)
pr.head: 8c282db3d88e2bec4924b280bf9867b050a1f042

summary: field keys <instrument> plays a SuperCollider instrument live from the computer keyboard or any MIDI controller. It starts a voice host: sclang, SuperCollider's language process, running Field's sc/voice-host.scd. The host boots its own scsynth audio server and plays the instrument's voice, the SynthDef its program returns when FIELD_MODE is voice. A recorded take renders offline through the same voice and the same voicer, sc/voicer.scd, which holds the rules that turn MIDI into voices.

Before this pull request, changing an instrument meant quitting field keys, editing the program, and starting again, which waits several seconds while scsynth boots. The modulation wheel (MIDI CC 1) did nothing, because the voice contract had no control for it. The keyboard-instrument plan deferred both, as §7 questions 5 and 6. This pull request answers them in a new §14:

• Saving the program reloads it. Field watches the program file. On a change, it sends an OSC message, /field/reload, to sclang's own UDP port, which Field now chooses and passes with -u. The host loads the program again with a new shared loader, sc/voice-load.scd. The next note plays the new voice, and notes already sounding finish on the old one. A save that does not load keeps the last good voice, and the instrument's line says why.
  • The wheel reaches the voice as mod. CC 1 divided by 127 becomes mod, an optional SynthDef control from 0 to 1. The voicer passes it to each new voice and sets it on every sounding voice when the wheel moves, live and in a take's render. juno turns it into vibrato, and bass into an opening filter.

§14.5 leaves three things for later. Acceptance criteria 37 to 41 need a real speaker and ears. A save in a session's first seconds can arrive before the host listens for it; that save is lost, and the next one reloads. And a take starts with the wheel at 0, because it records only what arrives once it has started, so you set the wheel again after the take starts.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Voice host: sclang running sc/voice-host.scd, started by field keys. It reports to Field in stdout lines that start @field , each one JSON object.
  • Voice: the SynthDef an instrument program returns in voice mode, with freq, amp, gate, out, and now an optional mod.
  • Voice mode and render mode: an instrument program checks FIELD_MODE. In voice mode it returns a voice; in render mode it renders a file under Field's sc-render contract.
  • Voicer: sc/voicer.scd, the MIDI-to-voices rules that the live host and the take render share.
  • Take render: the build's offline render of a recorded take through its instrument, by sc/voice-render.scd.
  • Harness: Field's own SuperCollider files that decide a take's sound, now voice-render.scd, voice-load.scd, and voicer.scd.
  • OSC: Open Sound Control, the UDP message format SuperCollider speaks.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
Two reviews so far:

  • At 286fe04, changes requested. Two findings: a take recorded with the wheel already up renders without it, and two doc edits broke the wrapping around them. It also suggested pointing plan §2.6 at §14, giving mod its own sentence in build-graph.md, and keeping only the first ERROR: line in voice-host.ts.
  • At 8c282db, clean. The branch was rebased onto main unchanged, and one commit answers the review. docs/keys.md and §14.5 now say a take starts with the wheel at 0, which is one of the two fixes the finding named. The paragraphs are reflowed, and all three suggestions are taken. Both findings are verified fixed and resolved.

The second review left one suggestion: §14.5 cites arming.md chunk 3, a plan that only #189, stacked above, adds.

groups.title: The voicer carries the mod wheel
groups.kicker: CC 1 becomes mod on every new and sounding voice, live and in renders
intro: The voicer is sc/voicer.scd: one function, shared by the live host and the take render, that turns MIDI into voices. Its caller passes callbacks that start, change, and release a voice. It returns an Event, SuperCollider's dictionary-like object, whose entries noteOn, noteOff, cc, bend, and forgetVoices the caller invokes as MIDI arrives.

CC 1 now sets mod, the wheel's value from 0 to 1. A new voice starts with the current mod, and a wheel move sets it on every voice in the voicer's table. To carry both pitch bend and mod, the callback that retuned a voice, setFreq.(voice, freq), becomes set.(voice, control, value).

checks.text: No new Event entry can collide with a built-in method. An entry named like a method of Event's class chain runs the method instead, as clear once did. The entries are unchanged, and set and mod are a closure argument and a local variable, which SuperCollider resolves lexically. The real-sclang voicer test prints from the set callback, so the callback is what runs.

files.note: The CC 1 branch, mod passed to start, and set in place of setFreq.

checks.text: A take's render starts here at mod = 0, and a take holds only messages that arrive after it starts. A wheel left up before the take plays live but not in the render, so docs/keys.md tells you to set it again after the take starts, and §14.5 records why carrying it waits.
The wheel reaches only voices still in voices. A released voice in its release tail has left the table, so a wheel move no longer reaches it, as a bend does not.

files.note: Through real sclang: a note starts with mod 0, CC 1 at 127 sets 1.0 on the sounding voice and starts the next with it, and CC 1 at 0 sets both back.

groups.title: One loader for every voice load
groups.kicker: sc/voice-load.scd: the first load, each reload, and the take render load a program the same way
intro: An instrument program is a SuperCollider file. In voice mode, when the environment variable FIELD_MODE is voice, its value, the file's last expression, must be a SynthDef. The host and the take render each ran the program with executeFile and checked the result themselves. They now share sc/voice-load.scd, a function of the program's path that answers [voiceDef, nil], or [nil, why].
The loader compiles before it runs, so a syntax error gets a reason of its own, juno.scd does not compile. A runtime error, and a value that is not a SynthDef, keep the reasons the host already gave.

files.note: The loader. It sets thisProcess.nowExecutingPath while the program runs, as executeFile does, so a program can find its own directory.

checks.text: compileFile answers nil for a syntax error, and sclang prints its own ERROR: line saying what is wrong. The loader's reason does not carry that line; src/keys/voice-host.ts attaches it on Field's side.
try keeps a runtime error from printing, so a reload that fails at run time reports only the loader's reason, with the error's own text in it.

groups.title: The live host reloads when Field asks
groups.kicker: An OSC responder in sc/voice-host.scd, and reload() in voice-host.ts
intro: The voice host is sclang running sc/voice-host.scd. It reports to Field on its standard output, where each line that starts @field is one JSON object, such as {"ready":true,…}. src/keys/voice-host.ts starts the host and parses those lines into statuses.

Field now picks a second free UDP port and starts sclang with -u <port>, so it knows where sclang listens. reload() sends /field/reload there. The host's responder accepts the message only from 127.0.0.1, loads the program again, and answers with one of two new lines:

• {"reloaded":true}: the new SynthDef is on the server, and the next note plays it.
  • {"reload_error":"…"}: the program did not load, and the last good voice still plays. Field attaches the first ERROR: line that sclang printed since the reload, which is where a syntax error is explained.

While the server is booting, at the first start or after a sample-rate restart, there is nothing to add the SynthDef to. The responder then only replaces voiceDef, which the boot adds once the server answers.

checks.text: A reload leaves sounding notes alone. An offline render replaced a SynthDef under a running node: the node kept its old sound, and a node started afterwards used the new definition. The voicer's held and sustained notes are not touched by a reload.
A reload's server.sync cannot hold up a rate restart's boot. In the installed SuperCollider, NetAddr.sync gives each call its own condition and responder, so the two syncs wait independently.

files.note: Loads with voice-load.scd at start and in the new /field/reload responder, and passes mod to each new Synth.

checks.text: Only a datagram from this machine reloads. Any local process can send one, but a reload only reads again the program Field named at start.
While booting, the responder swaps voiceDef without adding it to a server. The boot routine adds whatever voiceDef holds once serverRunning is true.

files.note: Chooses sclang's port, sends /field/reload, and turns the two new host lines into reloaded and reload-failed statuses.

checks.text: Only the first ERROR: line since the last reload() is kept, and that is the line a syntax error's reason gets.
-u fixes sclang's port. -D keeps sclang from reading standard input, which is why the plan rejected stdin as the reload channel.

files.note: The stub sclang listens on its -u port and answers reloads from STUB_RELOADS. The new case checks both answers, with sclang's error line attached, and that each reload reached the port.

groups.title: field keys watches the program and shows what each save did
groups.kicker: watchText, shared with the keymap watch, and the instrument's line
intro: field keys already reloaded a keymap given by path when you saved it. That watch moves unchanged from watchKeymap into src/keys/watch.ts, as watchText, and now also watches the instrument's program. It watches the file's directory, not the file, because many editors save by renaming a temporary file over the original, and a watch on the file would keep following the old one. It calls back only when the text has changed.

field keys shows the instrument on a line of its own above the status line. That line now also says what the last save did. A save that loaded adds · reloaded. A save that failed replaces the line with juno kept its last voice: …, which leads with the reason so a narrow terminal keeps it.

checks.text: The rename-on-save handling survives the move: the body is the old watchKeymap body line for line. The keymap reload tests, which re-save every 500 ms so a missed event cannot hang them, passed five runs of five.

files.note: watchKeymap now parses the text that watchText reads.
Starts the program watch, keeps each reload result beside the host's state, and draws it.

checks.text: The watch starts as soon as sclang is spawned. A save after the host has read the program, but before it registers its responder, is lost, and the next save reloads (§14.5).
A failed reload hides the live or restarting state until a save loads again.

groups.title: A take renders with the loader and the wheel
groups.kicker: voice-render.scd uses voice-load.scd and passes mod; the harness grows to three files
intro: A take is a recording of what you played, kept as a notes file. The build renders it offline through the instrument with sc/voice-render.scd, which turns the take's events into a score through the same voicer the live host uses. The take's CC 1 events now reach the voicer, so a wheel moved during the take moves mod in the render.

The render's cache key covers the program and Field's harness, the SuperCollider files that decide the sound. sc/voice-load.scd joins the harness, so a change to any of the three files renders every take again.

checks.text: A take holds only the messages that arrive after it starts, so a take's render starts with the wheel at 0. docs/keys.md "Record what you play" says so.

files.note: Loads with voice-load.scd, passes mod in each /s_new, and sets any control through set.

checks.text: Each harness file's SHA-256 is an input of the render, through extraInputs. So the changed voicer.scd and voice-render.scd re-render takes without a version bump.

files.note: Lists the new harness file among the inputs, and renders a voice whose level is mod: silent without CC 1, sounding with it.

groups.title: juno and bass respond to the wheel
groups.kicker: Vibrato on juno, an opening filter on bass, and render branches left as they were
intro: Both instruments in examples/bloom/shared/instruments/ are the JU-06A, a model of the Roland Juno's signal chain, set up two ways. Each builds its sound with ju06a.(freq, gate, k, mod), where k holds the instrument's fixed knob settings. Two new knobs say what the wheel does. modVibrato is the vibrato depth in semitones, at 5.5 Hz, and modOpen is how far the filter opens. juno gets half a semitone of vibrato, and bass opens its filter up to four times its cutoff.
Only the voice-mode SynthDef passes mod, smoothed over 50 ms. The render-mode branch calls ju06a with three arguments, so mod is nil there and the graph has neither term.

checks.text: The render branches are unchanged. juno and bass, rendered in render mode with seed 1 for 4 seconds in stereo and in mono, give the same SHA-256 at the merge base and at this head, with real sound (peaks from 0.34 to 0.53).
With mod at 0 the vibrato factor is 2 ** 0, exactly 1, so a voice with the wheel down plays the pitch it did before.

groups.title: The docs describe mod and reload, and the plan records §14
intro: docs/keys.md adds mod to the voice contract's table, describes reloading, and says that a take starts with the wheel at 0. docs/build-graph.md names sc/voice-load.scd as a third harness file and the wheel among what a take render plays. The plan points §7 questions 5 and 6, and §2.6's contract and its modulation bullet, at §14. §14 records what was built, four decisions with the alternatives they beat, criteria 37 to 41, what was verified, and what is still owed.

files.note: The mod row, reloading with an example of a failed save's line, what the wheel does on juno and bass, and the wheel at a take's start.

checks.text: The paragraph is reflowed: its lines now wrap near 70 columns, like the lines around them.
This is how the change answers a wheel set before a take: it states the limit. Pressing the same musical-typing key again sends its value again, because a set control sends at every press.

files.note: The optional mod control, and the take render's loader and three harness files.

checks.text: mod has a sentence of its own, so the clause about freeing the voice reads as the SynthDef's again.

files.note: §2.6 and §7 questions 5 and 6 point at §14, and §14 records the work.

checks.text: §14.5 lists checks still owed and one explicit deferral, not open questions, so the plan's in-progress status leaves nothing from this change unanswered.

arming.md is added by #189, which is stacked on this pull request, so main lacks it until #189 merges. Its chunk 3 is the lasting arm, but where that arm lives, the daemon or .field/, is still its §7 question 1. The review suggests naming the condition, the daemon keeping MIDI sources open between takes, rather than the chunk.
